entry: Film, literary, and media franchise centered on the British Secret Service agent [[James Bond (literary character)|James Bond]], code-named 007. Ian Fleming created the character in 1953, and other authors have written authorized Bond novels since Fleming's death. The Eon Productions film series began in 1962 with *Dr. No*, starring [[Sean Connery]], and had twenty-five films as of 2021. Its films have grossed over US$7.04 billion at the box office, making it the fifth-highest-grossing film series to date. Recurring features include the theme songs, Bond's cars, guns, and gadgets from Q Branch, and his relationships with women, known as "Bond girls." Three theme songs have received [[Academy Awards]].

Fictional British Secret Service officer, code-named 007. [[Ian Fleming]] created the character in 1953 and wrote twelve Bond novels and two short-story collections. Other authors later wrote Bond novels. Bond was a composite of commandos Fleming knew in the Naval Intelligence Division during the Second World War, to whom Fleming added his own style and tastes. His traits include a love of cars, food, drink, and sex, and an average intake of sixty custom-made cigarettes a day. His name may come from the American ornithologist James Bond, though Fleming may instead have taken it from a Welsh agent he served with.

American singer, songwriter, and record producer known as the "Godfather of Soul." Brown began as a gospel singer in Toccoa, [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], and rose to prominence in the mid-1950s as lead singer of the [[Rhythm and blues|rhythm and blues]] group the Famous Flames. His late-1960s music emphasized stripped-down, interlocking rhythms that influenced the development of [[Funk|funk]], which he fully established in the early 1970s with records such as "Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine." He was also noted for songs of social commentary, including "Say It Loud – I'm Black and I'm Proud" (1968). He recorded 17 singles that reached No. 1 on the Billboard R&B charts and was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1986. His music has been heavily sampled by [[Hip-hop|hip-hop]] musicians. He continued to perform until his death from pneumonia.

15th president of the United States (1857–61). A Democrat from Pennsylvania, Buchanan upheld a pro-slavery interpretation of the Constitution. Before taking office, he sought to secure the pro-slavery ruling in Dred Scott v. Sandford, and he supported admitting Kansas as a slave state under the Lecompton Constitution. In his last months in office, seven Southern states seceded, and on April 12, 1861, Confederate forces attacked Fort Sumter, starting the [[American Civil War]]. Critics in the North and South faulted his limited response to the secession crisis. Historians and scholars rank him among the worst presidents in American history.

American actor. He rose to prominence as Sonny Corleone in *The Godfather* (1972), earning Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations for Best Supporting Actor. He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 1978. Earlier roles included films by [[Howard Hawks]] and [[Francis Ford Coppola]], and his portrayal of Brian Piccolo in the television movie *Brian's Song* (1971) earned a Primetime Emmy Award nomination. After a five-year break from acting, he returned in films including *Misery* (1990), *Eraser* (1996), and *Elf* (2003).

Canadian and New Zealand filmmaker and explorer. His films combine cutting-edge technology with classical filmmaking techniques and have grossed over $10 billion worldwide, making him the second-highest-grossing film director of all time. He has received three Academy Awards, for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Film Editing for *Titanic* (1997). His earlier films include *The Terminator* (1984), *Aliens* (1986), and *Terminator 2: Judgment Day* (1991). In 2012 he became the first person to make a solo descent to the bottom of the [[Mariana Trench]], the deepest part of Earth's ocean, in the submersible *Deepsea Challenger*. A [[National Geographic]] explorer-in-residence, he has produced documentaries on deep-ocean exploration, and in 2010 [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world.

British experimental physicist who discovered the [[Neutron|neutron]]. Chadwick studied under [[Ernest Rutherford]] at Manchester and then at Cambridge, where he became Rutherford's assistant director of research. He spent four years in the Ruhleben internment camp in Germany during [[World War I]]. In 1941 he wrote the final draft of the MAUD Report, which inspired the U.S. government to begin serious atomic bomb research, and he headed the British team on the [[Manhattan Project]] during [[World War II]]. He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935 for discovering the neutron and was knighted in 1945. In 1935 he also became a professor of physics at Liverpool, where he installed a cyclotron.

American actor who appeared in more than 70 films, largely action roles. Coburn had leading roles in [[Western (genre)|Westerns]] and action films, including *The Magnificent Seven*, *The Great Escape*, *Our Man Flint*, and *Cross of Iron*. During the [[New Hollywood]] era he cultivated an image synonymous with "cool." He guest-starred in many television Westerns, including several episodes of [[Bonanza]] on [[NBC]]. In 1998 he won an [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for his supporting role as Glen Whitehouse in *Affliction*. He made 100 television appearances during a 45-year career.

British Royal Navy officer, explorer, and cartographer. Cook led three voyages of exploration in the [[Pacific Ocean]] and [[Southern Ocean]] between 1768 and 1779. He completed the first recorded circumnavigation of the main islands of [[New Zealand]], and his voyages included the first recorded European visit to Australia's east coast and the [[Hawaiian Islands]]. He claimed several territories for the [[Kingdom of Great Britain]] and made contact with numerous [[Indigenous peoples]]. His contributions to preventing [[Scurvy|scurvy]] earned him the Copley Gold Medal of the Royal Society. In 1779, during his second visit to Hawaii, he was killed in a violent dispute with Native Hawaiians. There is debate over the extent of his responsibility for violent encounters with Indigenous peoples, the transmission of infectious diseases, and his claims to Indigenous land without consent.

English actor, comedian, and television host. Corden co-wrote and starred in the [[BBC]] [[Sitcom|sitcom]] *Gavin & Stacey*, for which he won a BAFTA Television Award. He hosted *The Late Late Show with James Corden* on [[CBS]] from 2015 to 2023, and he created the Carpool Karaoke sketch in 2011. On Broadway he won a Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play for *One Man, Two Guvnors*. Corden has won 12 Primetime Emmy Awards from 29 nominations and was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in 2015 for services to drama.

American actor. He appeared in just three major films, *East of Eden* (1955), *Rebel Without a Cause* (1955), and *Giant* (1956), all preserved in the National Film Registry. He received posthumous Academy Award nominations for Best Actor for *East of Eden* and *Giant*, making him the only actor with two posthumous acting nominations. In 1999 the American Film Institute ranked him 18th among the greatest male film stars of Golden Age Hollywood. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named him one of the "All-Time Most Influential Fashion Icons" in 2012. He was killed in a car accident, and his image came to symbolize youthful rebellion.

American actor, known for his deep voice and as a pioneer for Black actors. He is one of the few performers to have won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony. He won two Tony Awards for Best Actor in a Play, for *The Great White Hope* and *Fences*, and acted in Shakespeare in the Park productions of *Hamlet* and *King Lear*. He served as an officer in the U.S. Army during the [[Korean War]]. His film debut was in [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s *Dr. Strangelove* (1964). He voiced [[Darth Vader]] in *Star Wars* and Mufasa in *The Lion King* (1994).

American criminal convicted of assassinating [[Martin Luther King Jr.]] in Memphis on April 4, 1968. After fleeing, he was captured in [[London]]. He pleaded guilty in 1969 to avoid a possible death sentence and received 99 years in prison, though he later tried to withdraw the plea. Ray supported segregationist [[George Wallace]] in 1968. A jury in a 1999 civil trial in Memphis concluded that King was the victim of a conspiracy. The King family has said it believes Ray was innocent, a view the U.S. Department of Justice disputed in 2000. He died of liver failure caused by [[Hepatitis C|hepatitis C]] after serving twenty-nine years in prison.

American actor. He was best known for playing Tony Soprano, an Italian-American mafia boss, in the [[HBO]] series *The Sopranos* (1999–2007), a role regarded as one of the most influential performances in television history. The role won him three Primetime Emmy Awards, five Actor Awards, and a Golden Globe. His films include *True Romance* (1993), *Get Shorty* (1995), and *Zero Dark Thirty* (2012). He earned an Actor Award nomination for the romantic comedy *Enough Said* (2013). On Broadway he appeared in *A Streetcar Named Desire* and was nominated for a Tony Award for *God of Carnage*.

American actor and producer of film and television. Garner was born James Scott Bumgarner. He became a television star as the gambler Bret Maverick in *Maverick* (1957–62), a role he reprised in *Bret Maverick* (1981–82). In the 1970s he starred as the private investigator Jim Rockford in *The Rockford Files* (1974–80). He also played leading roles in more than 50 theatrical films, including *The Great Escape* (1963) and *Murphy's Romance* (1985), for which he received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor. He won three Golden Globe Awards and two Primetime Emmy Awards.

French-British financier and politician. His controversial business career led to frequent clashes with British media, often involving litigation or the threat of it. The tabloid press described him as a greenmail corporate raider and asset stripper, a categorization he denied. Born in Paris, he fled France with his family when [[Nazi Germany]] overran the country. In 1994 he was elected to the European Parliament for a French constituency. He founded the short-lived Eurosceptic Referendum Party in the United Kingdom, an early campaigner against Britain's membership of the [[European Union]].

Scottish geologist, agriculturalist, and chemical manufacturer, often called the "Father of Modern Geology." Hutton inferred the remote history of the Earth from evidence in present-day rocks, studying features such as Salisbury Crags and Siccar Point. He argued that geological features underwent continuing transformation over indefinitely long periods, and he was one of the earliest proponents of uniformitarianism, the view that continuing natural processes shape the Earth's crust. He proposed a "system of the habitable Earth," a deistic mechanism to keep the world suitable for humans, an early form of the [[Anthropic principle]]. He earned a medical doctorate at Leiden University and co-owned a profitable chemical works that made sal ammoniac from [[Soot|soot]]. In Berwickshire he farmed and introduced innovative farming practices.

King of England, Scotland, and Ireland, 1685–88. The last Catholic monarch of the three kingdoms, James was deposed in the [[Glorious Revolution]]. He was the second surviving son of [[Charles I of England|Charles I]]. Parliaments in England and Scotland refused to pass measures undermining the Protestant religion, and his attempts to impose them by decree met opposition. In 1688 leading English politicians invited William of Orange, his nephew and son-in-law, to take the throne. After his defeat at the Battle of the Boyne in 1690, he returned to France, where [[Louis XIV]] protected him.

Irish novelist, poet, and literary critic. *Ulysses* (1922) is a landmark work that parallels the episodes of [[Homer]]'s *Odyssey* in a variety of literary styles, particularly stream of consciousness. Although Joyce spent most of his adult life abroad, in [[Trieste]], [[Zurich]], and [[Paris]], his fiction centers on [[Dublin]]. Publication of *Ulysses* was prohibited in the United Kingdom and the United States for its perceived obscenity until the mid-1930s. His other works include the short-story collection *Dubliners* (1914), the novel *A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man* (1916), and the experimental *Finnegans Wake* (1939). He died in Zurich after surgery for a perforated ulcer.

11th president of the United States (1845–49). A Democrat and protégé of [[Andrew Jackson]], Polk was an advocate of expansionism. Texas joined the Union in his first year, and the [[Mexican–American War]] that followed ended with Mexico ceding the American Southwest. He settled the Oregon boundary dispute with [[Great Britain]] along the 49th parallel. As he had pledged, Polk served one term and died of [[Cholera|cholera]] soon after leaving office. Scholars rank him in the middle to upper tier of presidents, but critics argue that his war with Mexico deepened sectional divides over slavery.

Founding Father and fourth president of the United States (1809–17). Madison was acclaimed the "Father of the Constitution" for his central role in drafting the [[Constitution]] and the Bill of Rights. He joined [[Alexander Hamilton]] and John Jay in writing *The Federalist Papers*, pro-ratification essays. Alongside [[Thomas Jefferson]], he organized the Democratic–Republican Party in opposition to Hamilton's [[Federalist Party]]. As Jefferson's secretary of state, he helped convince him to submit the [[Louisiana Purchase]] treaty to the Senate. He led the United States into the [[War of 1812]]. Born into a slave-owning planter family in [[Virginia]], he owned slaves at his plantation, Montpelier.

American painter and printmaker based mainly in the United Kingdom. Whistler rejected sentimentality and moral allusion in painting and was a leading proponent of "art for art's sake." He titled many paintings as "arrangements," "harmonies," and "nocturnes" to emphasize tonal harmony. His best-known work, *Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1* (1871), is commonly known as *Whistler's Mother*. He produced nearly 500 etchings, many of them of the Thames River. In 1878 he brought a libel suit against critic John Ruskin, winning a farthing in damages that left him bankrupt. His decorative harmony influenced [[Impressionism]], and he taught in [[Venice]] and Paris late in his career.

Founding Father and fifth president of the United States (1817–25). He was the last Founding Father to serve as president, and his presidency coincided with the Era of Good Feelings after the collapse of the [[Federalist Party]]. As President [[Thomas Jefferson]]'s envoy, he helped negotiate the [[Louisiana Purchase]]. In 1819 the Adams–Onís Treaty gave the United States Florida, and in 1823 Monroe announced the [[Monroe Doctrine]], opposing European intervention in the Americas. He signed the Missouri Compromise, which admitted Missouri as a slave state and banned slavery from territories north of the 36°30′ parallel. Liberia's capital, [[Monrovia]], is named in his honor.

English physicist and brewer. Joule studied the nature of heat and showed its relationship to mechanical work, leading to the law of [[Conservation of energy|conservation of energy]] and the [[First law of thermodynamics|first law of thermodynamics]]. He estimated the mechanical equivalent of heat as 4.1868 joules per [[Calorie|calorie]]. He worked with [[Lord Kelvin]] to develop an absolute thermodynamic temperature scale, which became known as the Kelvin scale. His finding on the relationship between the current through a [[Resistor|resistor]] and the heat dissipated is known as Joule's first law. Tutored as a young man by [[John Dalton]], he managed the family brewery as an adult, and the SI unit of energy, the [[Joule|joule]], is named after him.

American actor known for portraying morally ambiguous and eccentric characters. His breakthrough came in [[Steven Soderbergh]]'s drama *Sex, Lies, and Videotape* (1989), for which he won the Best Actor award at the [[Cannes Film Festival]]. He played the attorney Alan Shore in *The Practice* and its spin-off *Boston Legal*, earning three Primetime Emmy Awards. He later starred as Raymond Reddington in the [[NBC]] series *The Blacklist* (2013–2023), and he voiced the villain Ultron in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] film *Avengers: Age of Ultron* (2015).
